summary: This cycle is Claude Fable 5.2. The launch post and its 961-comment HN thread dwarf everything else, with Mythos still gated and Fable cheaper and faster than 5.1. The rest of the week argues about what sits around the model: Amazon's Strands Decider story (624 points) says a harness swap beat another Sonnet bill, Anthropic published a memory design that prefers a few good files over hundreds of notes, and Google shipped Omni 1.2 Flash plus Gemini 4 Carbon while catching a 696-point privacy story about Drive and Gmail going to human annotators. Meta's Muse Ember is aimed at cheap tool-call workers. Builder sentiment is splitting: one-shot games on one side, unread 100% AI codebases on the other.

highlights.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
highlights.why: Anthropic's Nov 9 drop is the week's actual headline: Fable 5.2 is cheaper ($8/$40 per million tokens), up to 30% faster than 5.1, optional 2.5x fast mode, and it became Claude Code's default. Mythos stays gated. HN's 961-comment thread is where builders are stress-testing it, not the duplicate 6-comment post.

highlights.title: Google Gemini routes personal Drive files and emails to human annotators
highlights.why: Privacy is now an agent-product issue, not a policy footnote. If Gemini can send Drive and Gmail content to human annotators, every agent with mailbox or docs access inherits that risk. 696 points says this landed harder than most model cards.

highlights.title: Amazon saves millions by replacing Sonnet 4.6 with Strands Decider
highlights.why: The week's strongest harness-over-model story. Amazon's public claim is cost, not a new frontier score: swap the decider layer, keep the rest of the agent, save millions. That matches the broader pattern that routing, memory, and tool gates move scores more than another model bump.

highlights.title: AlphaProof Code
highlights.why: Formal proof work leaking into coding agents is a different bet than autocomplete. If DeepMind is putting AlphaProof-style search on code, the interesting question is whether agent loops start treating tests and proofs as the same kind of verifier.

highlights.title: Fable 5.2 one-shotted my nephew's dream game
highlights.why: This is the consumer-side of the Fable drop: one long agent run, a finished artifact, 408 comments arguing about whether that is impressive or disposable. It is the same capability labs are selling as 18-hour unattended work.

highlights.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
highlights.why: Google's cheap multimodal worker for longer clips and lower price. For agent stacks this is a subagent model: video in, tools out, billed like Flash rather than the frontier coding models.

highlights.title: Claude Fable 5.2 scores 65 on Artificial Analysis, highest so far
highlights.why: Independent leaderboard confirmation of the launch, not Anthropic's own OSWorld number. Builders are using AA as the public scoreboard for whether a coding agent upgrade is real.

highlights.title: Muse Ember: Our smallest, most efficient model
highlights.why: Meta is pitching Ember as the cheap repeating worker: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction. That is the Haiku/Luna slot. If the cost curve holds, multi-agent graphs get a new default leaf model.

highlights.title: The Components of Agent Memory
highlights.why: Anthropic's engineering note is the week's best primary source on memory: transcripts vs notes vs navigable wikis, plus offline dreaming passes. The practical lesson is fewer well-kept files beat dumping hundreds of notes into context.

highlights.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
highlights.why: Carbon is Google's other model move this window, landing the day after Fable 5.2. For agent builders it is the question of whether Antigravity and Gemini CLI get a new default, not another chat model.

highlights.title: AI usage generates a fragile codebase
highlights.why: Counterweight to the one-shot demos. The comment thread is builders describing code they can ship and cannot maintain. Agent research that only tracks merge speed is missing this failure mode.

highlights.title: CodeRabbit scales agentic software development and ships 20x more
highlights.why: OpenAI's Codex distribution story this week: a review agent claiming 20x shipping, which is the enterprise version of the same Fable one-shot energy. Treat the multiplier as marketing, treat the shape (review agent in the loop) as real.

tangentRadar.whyItMatters: The largest cost and quality claims this week are about routing, memory, and retrieval, not a new weights file. If a decider or a search tool moves the bill more than the model, agent roadmaps that only track frontier releases are looking at the wrong layer.
Labs are selling hours-to-days of unattended work. Demos look like finished games and 20x shipping. The matching failure mode showed up in the same window: code nobody on the team can read.

signals: Fireworks / Notion vendor incident on HN
tangentRadar.whyItMatters: Once agents have mail, docs, and vendor tools, privacy incidents become product incidents. Annotator pipelines and third-party AI vendors are now in the same blast radius as the model.
Multi-agent graphs need a leaf model that is good at tool calls and cheap enough to spam. Ember, Omni Flash, and the Fable price cut are all aimed at that slot.
Proof search and wet-lab benchmarks both assume the agent can be checked. That is a different architecture than chat-with-tools.
The GitHub and Hugging Face side of the feed is still local CLIs and open checkpoints. They do not win HN, but they are what people run when APIs throttle.

experimentQueue.title: Run the same repo task on Fable 5.2 vs your current default
experimentQueue.why: The launch is cheap enough to A/B. Keep the harness fixed so you learn about the model, not about prompt drift.
experimentQueue.prompt: Same AGENTS.md, same repo, same ticket. Fable 5.2 vs last week's default. Compare diff quality, tokens, and whether a human can review the result.

experimentQueue.title: Trim agent memory to a handful of files
experimentQueue.why: Anthropic's memory note says organized notes beat volume. Most coding agents are still dumping transcripts into context.
experimentQueue.prompt: Take one long-running agent. Keep transcripts on disk, expose a small index, and add an offline pass that rewrites notes against the source files.

experimentQueue.title: Put a cheaper worker on tool calls
experimentQueue.why: Ember and Omni Flash are being sold as leaf models. If your planner is frontier-priced, your grep loop should not be.
experimentQueue.prompt: Route search, extraction, and browser subagents to a Flash/Ember-class model. Keep the planner on Fable or Carbon. Measure cost per merged PR.

experimentQueue.title: Audit one generated module for owners
experimentQueue.why: The fragile-codebase and 100% AI mandate threads are the same warning. Shipping speed is not the eval.
experimentQueue.prompt: Pick a module written mostly by agents in the last 90 days. Can two teammates explain it without the original session? If not, add tests and a human-owned map before the next agent pass.

method: HN Algolia search_by_date for created_at after 2026-11-04 with points > 80, plus title lookups for Fable 5.2, Gemini Omni 1.2, GPT-6 Cyber, and agent memory.
